draft.title: What productivity is
card: Productivity is how much is produced from the resources used. A common measure is labour productivity: output per hour worked.
Productivity rises when the same resources make more output, or when less resources make the same output.
Output alone is not productivity. A business can make more simply by hiring more workers, and its productivity may not change.
When productivity rises, a business can earn more from each hour of work. This can allow it to pay higher wages, and over time it can help living standards rise.
draft.remember: Productivity is output compared with inputs. More output per hour can support higher wages.

a.q: Which change shows a rise in labour productivity?
opts: A bakery makes 30 loaves an hour instead of 25
A bakery makes 250 loaves a day instead of 200
A bakery sells its loaves for more than last year
A bakery hires two extra staff and bakes more loaves
a.why: Labour productivity is output per hour worked, and 30 loaves an hour is higher than 25. Making 250 loaves a day instead of 200 is tempting, but the hours worked may have risen too, so productivity may not have changed.
a.clue: Look for output compared with hours worked.

b.q: Two farms in Tasmania each had 4 workers who worked 40 hours a week. Farm A packed 800 boxes of berries last week and Farm B packed 1,000. This week Farm A packs 1,000 boxes with 5 workers on the same hours. Which statement is correct?
opts: Farm B has higher labour productivity than Farm A
Farm A has higher labour productivity than Farm B
Both farms now have the same labour productivity
Farm A's productivity rose because its output rose
b.why: Farm B packs 1,000 boxes from 160 hours, while Farm A packs 1,000 boxes from 200 hours. Farm B gets more output per hour. Farm A's output rose, but it used more labour, so its output per hour did not rise.
b.clue: Work out the total hours for each farm first.

a.best: A bakery makes 30 loaves an hour instead of 25

b.best: Farm B has higher labour productivity than Farm A

problems.detail: '30 loaves an hour instead of 25' is output per clock hour, not output per hour worked. If the bakery added staff, labour productivity might not rise, which is the same trap the card warns about. Reword to something like 'makes 30 loaves per hour worked instead of 25' or 'the same staff make 30 loaves an hour instead of 25'.

The stem gives Farm B's figures only for last week. It never says Farm B's output or hours this week, yet the question and its why compare 'now'. State that Farm B still packs 1,000 boxes with 4 workers on 40 hours this week.
